### 1.  Work modulo \(63 = 7\cdot 9\)

Because \(63\) is not prime we treat the two prime factors separately.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
#### Modulo \(9\)

\(9\equiv0\pmod 9\), so for any positive exponent  

\[
9^{n}\equiv0\pmod 9 .
\]

Therefore  

\[
S\equiv0\pmod 9 .
\]

--------------------------------------------------------------------
#### Modulo \(7\)

\(9\equiv2\pmod 7\), thus  

\[
9^{\,10^{k}-1}\equiv2^{\,10^{k}-1}\pmod 7 .
\]

The order of \(2\) modulo \(7\) is \(3\) because \(2^{3}=8\equiv1\pmod 7\).  
Hence \(2^{m}\equiv2^{\,m\;(\bmod 3)}\pmod 7\).

Now \(10\equiv1\pmod 3\), so  

\[
10^{k}\equiv1^{k}\equiv1\pmod 3\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad
10^{k}-1\equiv0\pmod 3 .
\]

Thus each term satisfies  

\[
2^{\,10^{k}-1}\equiv2^{0}\equiv1\pmod 7 .
\]

There are \(600\) terms, so  

\[
S\equiv600\equiv5\pmod 7 .
\]

--------------------------------------------------------------------
#### Combine by the Chinese Remainder Theorem

We need \(x\) such that  

\[
x\equiv0\pmod 9,\qquad x\equiv5\pmod 7 .
\]

Write \(x=9a\). Then \(9a\equiv5\pmod 7\Rightarrow2a\equiv5\pmod 7\).

Hence  

\[
a\equiv5\cdot4\equiv20\equiv6\pmod 7,
\]

so \(a=6+7t\) and  

\[
x=9a=9(6+7t)=54+63t .

\boxed{54}.
